headline: Buffalo Bills Debut New Stadium with a 41-31 Victory Over Detroit Lions

sources.excerpt: Buffalo Bills debut new stadium, beating Detroit Lions in home opener. The Bills mafia enjoyed their new $2 billion Highmark Stadium, just outside Buffalo, in a game against the Detroit Lions with quarterback Josh Allen scoring five touchdowns. It's safe to assume the Buffalo Bills had some fun during Thursday night's victory over the Detroit Lions. After jumping out to a 21-0 lead early in the second quarter, each time the Lions managed to cut the lead to 10, the Bills quickly responded with a touchdown of their own. The Bills appeared to have complete control of the prime-time matchup from start to finish and were led by another stellar performance from Josh Allen. While Allen racked up 248 passing yards, 69 rushing yards and five total touchdowns, he even managed to find time to do a bit of lighthearted trolling on the field. A hot mic caught Allen just before a snap, literally asking the Detroit defensive line if it was going to jump offside. Considering the Bills were a stellar 9-of-12 on third-down attempts and racked up 34 total first downs, it's easy to see why Allen was having some fun throughout Thursday's game. The Bills dominated every important statistical category, including the aforementioned third-down conversions and total first downs, as well as total yards (446 vs. 355), red-zone efficiency (Buffalo was 5-of-5), and time of possession (33:45 to 26:15). The Bills offense appears to be at the top of the class in the NFL through two games, and it'll be fun to see if they can keep throwing haymakers as the season rolls on.

Buffalo Bills Defeat Detroit Lions 41 31 in Stadium Debut. Quarterback Josh Allen threw three touchdown passes and ran for two scores as the Buffalo Bills earned a 41-31 home victory over the Detroit Lions in the regular-season debut at their new $2.1 billion facility. Allen opened the scoring with a 1-yard touchdown run, later adding a 2-yard rushing score that tied him with Jim Taylor for 18th on the NFL all-time list with 83 career rushing touchdowns. Reflecting on the pregame moments prior to kickoff, the Buffalo quarterback noted the significance of the occasion. "I caught myself taking it all in an understanding how cool what I get to do. My job is the coolest in the world," Allen said. "It's everything I ever wanted, to be the quarterback of an NFL franchise. I'm just very fortunate to have ended up in Buffalo."

Buffalo's offensive output started strong by scoring on its first four drives, including touchdown catches by Josh Palmer, Dawson Knox, and Dalton Kincaid. Head coach Joe Brady expressed confidence by choosing to receive the opening kickoff after winning the coin toss. "Anytime the ball's in his hands, good things happen. And yeah, love that guy," Brady said.

Bills celebrate new Highmark Stadium in style with big win. The Buffalo Bills threw a heck of a housewarming party for their new Highmark Stadium on Thursday, launching fireworks to open the night and then piling up points in a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions that felt more dominant than the final score indicated. The Bills are 2-0, making Joe Brady the first coach in franchise history to win his first two games. Brady said he felt little emotion during the festivities -- that was on purpose; he wanted his players to remain composed, too -- but that wasn't the case for everyone else in Orchard Park, New York. Fans spent hours tailgating before the game and erupted when Hall of Famer Bruce Smith led them in a "Let's Go, Buffalo" chant.
